sanity_expectations: theta is finite and real across the entire sampled S-H region
at fixed H, theta rises from a low baseline through a sigmoidal transition near S~K and levels to a finite asymptote
theta stays bounded roughly within [0, 1.5] over the region
increasing proton level H raises the effector-driven contributions (alpha basal, delta offset, rho enhancement)
as S grows large at fixed H, theta approaches ~1 - gamma + delta*(H - Href)
excitation_report: sigma=0.01, k=5 (target 5*sigma=0.05). All six additive terms clear the threshold: baseline S**n/(K**n+S**n) 88.8x; delta proton-shift term 19.2x; NEW rho term 18.1x (RMS) with peak effect 33.3x sigma, strongest at S=2.18, H=4.85; gamma self-inhibition 15.2x; alpha basal-occupancy 6.5x; beta overshoot 6.5x. auto_balance rescaled alpha 0.20->0.303 and beta 0.30->0.655 so the two weakest terms reach 5*sigma; no weak terms remain.

H: V->V (confirmed proton/effector-level sampling axis; drives alpha, delta, rho terms)
n: V->P (overridden: cooperativity Hill exponent, fixed constant not an axis)
K: V->P (overridden: apparent half-saturation constant, fixed not an axis)
beta: P->P (confirmed; value tuned for excitation)
alpha: P->P (confirmed; value tuned for excitation)
rationale: Structure has no derivatives or integral kernels and is explicitly solvable for theta, so this is a static explicit relation evaluated on a 2D grid of the two physical axes S (substrate) and H (proton/effector). All remaining free symbols are fixed parameters; n and K were mislabeled as axes and were overridden to parameters. Parameter magnitudes follow standard cooperative-enzyme values (Hill exponents n=m=2, K=Ka=1, Ki=5 for the low-affinity inhibitory site). rho=0.5 uses the top of the suggested range; alpha and beta were auto-balanced upward so every term is visible above sigma=0.01 noise. All terms including the new proton-conditioned rho enhancement clear 5*sigma.

scenario_text: A multimeric enzyme with several interacting subunits shows a sigmoidal dependence of activity on substrate because substrate binding to one site enhances binding at others. At low substrate the response is shallow, then it rises sharply through a transition region before leveling off. Cooperativity strength governs the steepness of this switch-like transition. The objective is to describe fractional activity as a function of substrate concentration.
